title: [Issue]: Items added to Collections have completely disappeared.
body:
### Please describe your bug

I created an extensive collection list and now items added to those collections are completely gone. The xml files are blank slates as well. I have not made any changes to anything settings wise and this appears to be completely out of the blue.

### Reproduction Steps

Unknown

### Jellyfin Version

10.9.0

### if other:

```markdown
- OS:Ubuntu 22.04
- Linux Kernel: 6.5.0-35-generic 
- Browser:Firefox
- FFmpeg Version:

- Hardware Acceleration:None
- GPU Model:
- Plugins: AudioDB, Bookshelf, Fanart, Intros, IMDB, Playback Reporting, Reports, SkinManager, TVmaze, The TVDB, Theme Songs
- Reverse Proxy:
- Base URL:
- Networking:Host
- Storage:local
```

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I was wondering, given that it's intended for items to be removed from collections if the file no longer exists, would there be a way to make that behavior a bit smarter? 

It was probably intended so that when movies get deleted, there are no remains somewhere in the collections and playlists. 

Given that quite a few of the issues seem to happen when for whatever reason the media directory isn't correctly mounted when Jellyfin starts (this just happened to me, too), could a check be added that checks if it's not literally deleting every single movie from every single collection (as it would when all the movies aren't available), and then skips cleanup and prints a log?

I can't imagine a situation where that (cleaning up *all* collections when *all* the movie files are gone) is user-expected behavior. 

Yes, I can remove the scheduled trigger (and just did so), but that's A) something everyone needs to do manually, and B) removing movies that are truly really gone and deleted from collections is useful so I do still need to run this from time to time.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
I ran into this issue a few days ago too. Actually, this is the second time it happened to me within the past few years but the first time I was too busy to investigate. According to the Windows system event log, the reason is that an HDD didn't come back up after a power failure.

Unfortunately I'm not familiar with C# but I believe I found the source of this serious bug.

It's in CleanupCollectionAndPlaylistPathsTask.cs (https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/916e897ed25f74b0112e51758e673f18ad13af1d/Emby.Server.Implementations/ScheduledTasks/Tasks/CleanupCollectionAndPlaylistPathsTask.cs#L115), line 115.

`if (!File.Exists(path) && !Directory.Exists(path))`

Items are removed when they neither exist as a file nor a folder, which is incorrect.

Correct would be (in pseudo code, and in this order):
if ( !FileExists (...) && !DirectoryExists (...) && !BaseFolderNameConfiguredInAnyLibrary (...) )

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
> [@participant4](https://github.com/participant4) that is intended behaviour though.

That's pretty much like saying rsync is supposed to delete the target when the source is not available.

If this is intended behaviour then it's not a bug, it's a serious design flaw.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
> Correct would be (in pseudo code, and in this order): if ( !FileExists (...) && !DirectoryExists (...) && !BaseFolderNameConfiguredInAnyLibrary (...) )

This is wrong too. :)

- Deletion can happen when the base folder exists and it is configured in a library under "Folder".
Or:
- Deletion can happen when the base folder does not exist and is not configured in a library under "Folder".

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I don’t know if @participant11 was that abusive. Does this version help?

If this is “by design,” then it’s still a design flaw. Deleting user data without consent is always wrong — that’s a very basic principle. As was pointed out earlier, it’s like saying rsync should delete the target if the source becomes unavailable.

Saying it’s the user’s responsibility to make sure Jellyfin has access at all times doesn’t really address the issue. The fact remains: Jellyfin deletes data when it shouldn’t. That happens not because users did something wrong, but because the current implementation makes assumptions that lead to data loss.

It should be possible to distinguish between cases like:
	•	The base folder exists and is configured in a library.
	•	The base folder doesn’t exist and isn’t even configured.

In other situations, deletion should never occur. That’s not complicated — it’s just common sense.

And this isn’t really a “feature request.” Preventing unintended deletion is not a feature, it’s a safeguard. Data loss is always a bug, even if it happens through flawed design.

comments.author: Shadowghost
comments.body:
> That happens not because users did something wrong, but because the current implementation makes assumptions that lead to data loss.

We are not responsible for data not being there anymore, that's the user's responsibility.

Sure, implementing a "soft delete" would be preferable but the current scanner and DB just wouldn't work with that. Don't misunderstand: We want to have this but there are bigger bugs and issues to squash, so this won't be something implemented any time soon.

AFAIK we are already skipping removal of data from the library on scans if the root folder is missing, but the collections and playlist cleanup task is independent of that. If you don't like the behaviour, just remove the scheduled task, but then removed items would never be cleaned up automatically.
We'd need to check if we can re-use the logic we use to skip on scan also in this task as a workaround.
But IMO this skipping is still a hack to workaround faulty user setups where mounts disappear or are not mounted properly on boot. 
We (the application) just consume what we can "see", if we don't, we delete . We don't (and should not need to) care if we don't see data because the mount failed, you removed it or the permissions are too restrictive, from an application point of view all of this is the same and the responsibility of the user and/or the OS.

> Not deleting a collection when it is completely empty and not updating a colection when an item returns to to the library doesn't.

1st thing can be added, 2nd thing is not so simple because collections reference internal items, once that is gone, we don't know about it any more. To make it work, there would need to be quite some changes:
a) Your first point would prevent the re-population if the collections are not created by e.g. the boxset plugins automatically
b) Instead of the path, we'd need to save internal and external IDs of associated items and don't delete the external Ids on removal of the internal item (similar to what we do with watched data) and re-attach once an item is scanned in with the same external ID. This is more or less a rewrite of the whole feature and will happen when we make collections database-only entities.

comments.author: participant15
comments.body:
I finally recovered my old collections. In case someone ends up doing the same, the XML files in the collection dirs are not the used data, they are generated on startup from the DB.

So if your collection is wiped, a db restore is probably the fastest way to go if you have a recent one. 

It took me a while to notice they were gone and longer to do anything about it so I didn't want to restore the DB, which had had a bunch of changes version upgrades so it was probably incompatible anyway. So I ended up updating it based on the the backed up XMLs. [Here's a crude bash script ](https://gist.github.com/participant15/6d29d1563af761659defe4f330a4abad)I used - it worked for me, but I haven't tested it beyond that.

Now that I think of it using the old DB as the source instead of the XMLs could have made more sense, but I guess I was still in the mindset that the XMLs were where they were "stored". So if you script this yourself that's probably the smart way to go instead of mine.
